prompt:
Orchestrator-driven on-demand agent spawning: lift the event pump out of the pod so idle agents don't exist.

## Summary

Today the orchestrator spawns the full agent team for a phase up front, and each agent pod then runs a long-lived in-pod event-pump loop (`orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py`) that long-polls the message bus and invokes the agent process one-shot per actionable BRC event. The pod stays alive — idle, heartbeating — for the whole phase, even while it has nothing to do, until global consensus fires.

This issue inverts that lifecycle: the orchestrator owns the event loop and spawns an agent pod only when that role has an actionable event; the pod handles the one event and exits. No idle pods.

Two goals: (1) Reduce resource use — idle pods hold CPU/memory reservation, gateway session, 30s heartbeat for the whole phase. (2) Make the system truly event-driven — the orchestrator already computes when a role is actionable (`_derive_next_action` in `orchestrator/routes/consensus.py`) but that signal is consumed by an in-pod bash loop. The orchestrator should push (spawn in direct response to the event) instead of every pod pulling.

This is resource-freeing, not latency-sensitive. No cold-start SLO. Per-phase reuse of prompt-cache prefix / gateway session / worktree is unchanged; pods just don't exist while a role is idle.

## Current state

- Spawn: at phase start, `concurrent_executor.spawn_all` → `kubernetes_spawner.spawn_agent_job` spawns one Job per role simultaneously, each wrapped by `build_consensus_wrapped_command`.
- Run: deterministic bash loop. Each iteration calls `egg-orch brc get-state` / `brc next-action`; on propose/ack/nack invokes the agent one-shot, on wait blocks on `egg-orch message wait-loop` (60s inner timeout) with a 30s heartbeat. Pod does not exit between events. confirm/complete handled agent-free.
- Terminate: only on global consensus (`is_complete=True`); 30-min idle budget raises OVERSEER_ALERT but does not terminate.

## Foundation already on main (#2908 / PR #2949)

- Stateless per-event invocation via `compose_event_prompt` (`orchestrator/routes/event_prompt.py`).
- Durable per-role continuity via BRC memory artifact (`.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md`, carrying `last_reviewed_commit_sha`).
- Cache-preserving prompt shape — prefix cache is server-side, not pinned to a pod; a fresh pod with the same stable prefix hits the same warm cache.
- Worktree persistence — hostPath-persistent across pod restarts, keyed per `{pipeline_id}[-{slice_id}]-{role}` (#3005, #2403).

## Desired model

- Make `_derive_next_action` the spawn trigger: when a role transitions from `wait` to an actionable verb, spawn a pod for it; otherwise no pod.
- Agent pod becomes a one-shot event handler: spawned with the composed per-event prompt, does the single unit of work, exits.
- Not every actionable verb needs a pod. Only propose/ack/nack spawn a pod. confirm/complete bookkeeping moves orchestrator-side.
- The wait lives in the orchestrator, not in a fleet of blocked pods.

## Scope (decided): Option B minus the latency SLO

- Orchestrator-side event loop + on-demand spawner for propose/ack/nack; confirm/complete executed orchestrator-side with no pod.
- An ownership flag (e.g. `EGG_EVENT_LOOP_OWNER`) that defaults to the in-pod loop; the flip to orchestrator-owned is a separate, gated follow-up (#3164), NOT part of this work.
- Failure supervision re-homed.
- Worktree re-attach + gateway-session reuse across a role's successive spawns — justified by correctness and resource hygiene, not a latency budget. A one-shot pod killed mid-event must not leak uncommitted/dirty residue into a successor's commit.
- Idle/stall alerts and health-monitor thresholds made lifecycle-owner-aware.
- Docs for the final shape.

The default flip and in-pod-loop retirement are explicitly out of scope (tracked in #3164, flip gated on a live BRC proving run with the flag on).

## Hard constraint for planning (learned from prior attempts)

The passive-wrapper coexistence guard and the on-demand spawner MUST land together — in the same deployable unit, or with the spawner strictly first. The #3023 run committed the ownership guard alone and had to revert: silencing the in-pod loop with nothing to replace it deadlocks BRC consensus. A plan that separates them must make the guard depend on the spawner, never the reverse. This matters more because `EGG_BRC_EVENT_PUMP` was deleted entirely in #2908 slice-4, so the wrapper has no rollback path. The new flag must default to the in-pod loop and flip only after the spawner is proven (the #3164 follow-up).

## Open considerations (for refine/plan to work through)

- Spawn idempotency. The consensus poll re-derives the same actionable event during a pod's ~10–30s startup; the spawner needs a dedupe key. Event identity is known: `proposal_commit_sha` (carried in `pending_reviews`, `routes/consensus.py:220`) for review verbs; target version + open NACK set for proposes. At most one live pod per role+slice.
- Durability across orchestrator restarts. Recommended: stateless re-derivation rather than persisted bookkeeping — on restart re-derive next-actions from the consensus tracker (rebuilt from the message store, #2761) and reconcile against live Kubernetes Jobs before spawning, with the dedupe key making re-derived spawns idempotent. The dedupe key must be derivable from durable state (message-store versions / commit SHAs), never from orchestrator process memory alone. (cf. #3070)
- Failure supervision. A one-shot pod that dies mid-event leaves nothing running — the orchestrator must respawn (bounded) or alert. #2806's exit-code path needs a new home. Recommended: bounded automatic respawn with backoff mirroring the wrapper's #3138 streak semantics; OVERSEER_ALERT only on persistent exhaustion. Distinguish pod-infrastructure failure from a legitimate NACK loop — only the former consumes respawn budget.
- Worktree reuse across successive spawns. Re-attach a role's existing worktree (validate expected branch / `.git` integrity / no foreign lock; fall back to create-with-retry on mismatch) and, on every successful re-attach, discard uncommitted/untracked residue and hard-sync to the role branch tip before invocation.
- Gateway session model. Reuse sessions across a role's successive spawns (re-register only when none is live or token aged out) with teardown at phase end / supervision exhaustion.
- Where the event loop / wait moves. The orchestrator already runs a consensus poll loop and next-action derivation; this is about wiring that to pod lifecycle.
- Re-homing the wrapper's responsibilities. The wrapper's heartbeat, idle budget, and per-event invocation need re-homing or retiring. Idle-budget overseer alert fits orchestrator-side; health-monitor heartbeat/container tripwires (which assume long-lived pods) must become lifecycle-owner-aware so "role has no pod" is treated as normal under orchestrator ownership.

## Recommended resolutions carried from the prior run's gates

- Scope: Option B, with the flip deferred to #3164.
- Failure-supervision policy: bounded automatic respawn with backoff mirroring #3138, OVERSEER_ALERT only on persistent exhaustion.

## Out of scope

- The agent primitive itself (pod image / worktree / Agent SDK / permissions / gateway restrictions).
- BRC protocol semantics (propose/ack/nack/confirm, Delphi redaction, multi-reviewer NACK barrier) — only when a pod exists changes.
- The default flip and in-pod-loop retirement — tracked in #3164.
- Extended prompt-cache TTL configuration.

## History

Supersedes #3064 (and before it #3023). Nothing from either attempt is on main; this is a clean re-run. The failure modes that sank #3023 are fixed on main: contract-verify skipping slice PRs (#3040 → #3048), post-BRC reviewer-confirm deadlock (#3043 → #3050), overlapping-but-unordered slices now rejected at plan ingestion (#3046 → #3049).

## Related

- #3164 — flip event-loop ownership to orchestrator + retire the in-pod wait arm (gated follow-up).
- #2908 (closed) — BRC event-pump + durable agent memory; the foundation (PR #2949 added `compose_event_prompt`).
- #3017 — declarative phase/stage abstraction. #2958 — streaming per-task commits. #2866 — k3s as the sole runtime.
